meta.title: ThermGAS U.S. Competitive Intelligence - Phase 4 analysis
meta.disclaimer: Independent student research by Northeastern University MSBA students. Not an official ThermGAS publication. Vendor specifications are vendor claims unless stated otherwise; no laboratory testing was performed.

headline_findings.title: Two verified direct competitors: ION Science and Riken Keiki/RKI
headline_findings.body: Both officially market fixed detectors for Li-ion battery manufacturing with DMC named as a target: ION Science FALCO 2 11.7 lists 'Li-ion Battery Manufacturing'; Riken Keiki lists DMC/EMC/DEC monitors for electrolyte filling and claims >10,000 detectors at Li-ion plants worldwide.
headline_findings.so_what: These are the vendors a battery-plant EHS buyer will compare ThermGAS against. Neither publishes a DMC detection limit under stated conditions - a published, test-conditioned DMC spec would be a differentiator.

headline_findings.title: The 11.7 eV PID trade-off is documented by the competitor itself
headline_findings.body: FALCO 2 11.7 reads DMC well (RF 1.50) but its lamp lasts up to 4 months (3-month lamp warranty) and a PID responds to every compound below 11.7 eV, so it cannot tell DMC from IPA or ethanol. The 10.6 eV TVOC 2 barely sees DMC (RF 60).
headline_findings.so_what: ThermGAS's strongest evidence-backed angle is selectivity plus maintenance burden - but the cost side must be proven with real lamp and labor quotes.

headline_findings.title: Honeywell sells event detection into the same gigafactory budget
headline_findings.body: Li-ion Tamer Gen 3 detects off-gas venting (10 ppm/s rate threshold, FM 6540) and Honeywell packages it with VESDA as a 'Gigafactory Fire Solution'. It does not report DMC concentration.
headline_findings.so_what: Position ThermGAS as a complement (continuous DMC concentration in filling / electrolyte-handling rooms), not as a rival 'earliest warning' device.

headline_findings.title: ThermGAS's own DMC evidence has gaps
headline_findings.body: Battery webpage says 0.5 ppm; the DMC application note says 1 ppm; DMC is absent from the Master Gas List; no interference data, no hazardous-area rating and no public battery-plant reference were found.
headline_findings.so_what: Fixing the spec sheet is the cheapest, highest-impact action before any sales push.

headline_findings.title: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference
headline_findings.body: The only verified U.S. installation reference in this category is a Honeywell Li-ion Tamer BESS site (Long Beach, CA) - not a factory.
headline_findings.so_what: The first credible U.S. reference site is still up for grabs.
headline_findings.status: Verified (absence of evidence after search, not proof of absence)

headline_findings.title: Competitor local presence is thin where battery capacity is concentrated
headline_findings.body: Verified competitor offices/distributors cluster in CA, TX and the Northeast; the largest announced cell capacity sits in KY, NV, MI, OH, TN and GA, where only GA (ION distributor) and OH/IN (inferred) show competitor channel evidence.
headline_findings.so_what: This is 'not verified', not 'no competition' - national vendors can still sell there - but it marks where channel research and early customer development pay off most.

battlecards.title: ION Science FALCO 2 11.7 eV
battlecards.their_pitch: Fixed 11.7 eV PID that 'sees' high-ionization VOCs incl. DMC; ATEX/IECEx/UL Zone 1; listed for Li-ion battery manufacturing.

where_they_win.text: Low, published entry price: $3,521 reseller list (diffused unit).
Hazardous-area approvals (UL Class I Zone 1, ATEX, IECEx) for installation in classified areas.
Strong DMC response at 11.7 eV (RF 1.50) and 0.1 ppm sensitivity (isobutylene basis).
U.S. office (Stafford, TX) plus distributors tagged in 10 states.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Selectivity: PAIR targets DMC's IR absorption; a PID sums every compound below 11.7 eV (IPA, ethanol, methanol) - fewer nuisance alarms in mixed-solvent rooms.
where_thermgas_can_win.status: Inferred (from documented principles; no head-to-head test)

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Maintenance: FALCO lamp lifetime up to 4 months (3-month lamp warranty) vs. no UV lamp / no depletable sensor in PAIR; Haloguard pump life typically 5-6 years.
Coverage: one Haloguard IR scans up to 24 sample points (500 ft tubing) vs. one FALCO per point (diffusion).

landmines.text: ThermGAS has no published hazardous-area rating; electrolyte rooms may be classified (DMC flash point ~17 C).
Multi-point scanning means each point is revisited only once per cycle (<1 min per channel) - slower per-point update than a dedicated PID (T90 60 s).
ThermGAS DMC spec is inconsistent (0.5 vs 1 ppm).

discovery_questions: Which other solvents (IPA, ethanol, EMC/DEC, NMP) are present in the room, and how often do you get nuisance VOC alarms?
Who replaces PID lamps today, how often, and what does each visit cost?
Is the monitored area electrically classified, and could an analyzer sit outside it with sample lines?
evidence_gaps: 11.7 eV lamp price and replacement labor
FALCO installed base in U.S. battery plants

battlecards.title: Riken Keiki / RKI Instruments
battlecards.their_pitch: Gas detection for every Li-ion process step (NMP drying, electrolyte filling, testing, separator); >10,000 detectors at Li-ion plants worldwide; 20+ years in the industry.

where_they_win.text: Breadth: one vendor for NMP duct monitors (up to 200 C), filling-area solvent monitors, test-area and O2 monitors.
Battery credibility: claims >10,000 detectors at Li-ion production sites and a ppm-level filling-area case study.
U.S. subsidiary RKI (Union City, CA) and factory-authorized service via PK Safety.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: DMC specificity: Riken's filling monitors are combustible (hot-wire) or NDIR types with no published DMC limit; ThermGAS can publish a DMC-specific ppm spec.
Low-ppm focus: hot-wire combustible sensors are designed for %LEL ranges; low-ppm DMC trend monitoring is a different job.
where_thermgas_can_win.status: Inferred (sensor principle; Riken ppm customisation exists)

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Multi-point extractive sampling from one analyzer.

landmines.text: Riken's case study shows it will customise ranges to ppm for filling customers - do not assume it cannot do low ppm.
Large Asian-OEM battery makers may already standardise on Riken globally.

discovery_questions: Is your gas-detection vendor specified by your global/parent-company standard?
Do you need a %LEL fire-safety alarm, a ppm exposure/leak trend, or both?
What does your current filling-area detector actually read when DMC is present at a few ppm?
evidence_gaps: DMC range/LOD for SD-1RI and SD-D58

battlecards.title: Honeywell Li-ion Tamer Gen 3
battlecards.their_pitch: Earliest off-gas (cell venting) detection, calibration-free, >10-year life, FM 6540 approved; sold with VESDA as a Gigafactory Fire Solution.

where_they_win.text: Brand, fire-system channel and certifications (FM 6540; CSFM listing for Gen2+).
Calibration-free, 10+ year life, bump test with a DEC bottle.
Scales to 100 sensors per controller for rack-level coverage.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: It reports a rate-of-change event, not DMC ppm: no concentration trend for leak hunting, exposure records or process-area alarms.
Designed around battery racks and air streams (monitoring + reference sensors) - a weaker fit for electrolyte-handling or filling rooms.

landmines.text: Bundled into fire-protection projects that ThermGAS may never see; buyer is fire/EHS, budget set early in plant design.
U.S. product page lists Gen 3 as 'Discontinued' while datasheet is current - check before claiming anything about its status.

discovery_questions: Is off-gas event detection already specified by the fire-protection designer?
Who owns electrolyte-leak monitoring in filling/handling rooms - EHS, process or facilities?

battlecards.title: Cubic ATRS-1050 (NDIR module)
battlecards.their_pitch: Low-cost NDIR sensor module for DMC/EMC/EC electrolyte leakage and thermal runaway.

where_they_win.text: DMC-specific optical sensing in a small OEM module with <1 s response (catalog).

where_thermgas_can_win.text: Accuracy at low ppm: ATRS-1050 is +/-200 ppm from 0-2,000 ppm; ThermGAS claims 0.5-1 ppm sensitivity.
Complete monitoring system (alarms, relays, BACnet, multi-point) vs. a component needing integration.

landmines.text: System integrators could build low-cost DMC monitors on Cubic modules; North American JV formed Dec 2025.

discovery_questions: Is your requirement a leak/thermal event alarm or a low-ppm concentration trend?

battlecards.title: MSA Chillgard 5000 (core-market watch)
battlecards.their_pitch: PAIR refrigerant monitor, 1 ppm, 4/8/16 points, BACnet/Modbus, 2-year warranty.

where_they_win.text: Same PAIR principle with published accuracy (+/-1 ppm 0-50 ppm), longer tubing (up to 1,250 ft) and 2-year warranty.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: No DMC on Chillgard's 37-refrigerant gas list - ThermGAS is first PAIR vendor marketing DMC.

landmines.text: MSA could add DMC to a PAIR platform; ThermGAS's technology claim alone is not a moat.

discovery_questions: Do you already run MSA/Bacharach refrigerant monitors on site?
evidence_gaps: Current Chillgard status (UK page shows X30/X50)

battlecards.title: INFICON ELT3000 (substitute at the source)
battlecards.their_pitch: End-of-line mass-spectrometer leak test that finds electrolyte-leaking cells before they leave the line.

where_they_win.text: Catches leaking cells (1e-6 mbar.l/s He-equivalent) before storage/aging; DMC check reference available.

where_thermgas_can_win.text: ELT3000 tests products, not room air - it does not cover spills, fittings, transfer lines or electrolyte storage.

landmines.text: Plants that invest in 100% cell leak testing may see less need for ambient DMC alarms in aging areas.

discovery_questions: Do you leak-test every cell, and where do leaks still reach the room air?

recommendations.title: Publish one test-conditioned DMC specification
recommendations.action: Resolve 0.5 vs 1 ppm; add DMC to the Master Gas List; publish detection limit, calibration gas, response time per point, and cross-sensitivity to IPA, ethanol, EMC, DEC and NMP.
recommendations.business_case: Neither direct competitor publishes a DMC limit; a credible spec turns ThermGAS's technology claim into a buyer-verifiable advantage.
recommendations.limitation: Requires ThermGAS lab data; results could narrow the advantage if interferents affect PAIR.
recommendations.next_step: Ask the sponsor for DMC calibration and interference test records.

recommendations.title: Position as the DMC-concentration layer that complements event detection
recommendations.action: Message: 'Know how much DMC is in the room, continuously' for electrolyte storage, mixing, transfer and filling rooms - alongside (not instead of) off-gas event systems.
recommendations.business_case: Honeywell owns the 'earliest event warning' story in gigafactories but reports a rate, not ppm; PIDs report ppm but not DMC specifically.
recommendations.limitation: Whether buyers budget for both layers is unverified.
recommendations.next_step: Test the message in 5-8 interviews with battery-plant EHS/process engineers.

recommendations.title: Answer the hazardous-area question before buyers ask
recommendations.action: Document how a remote analyzer with sample lines serves classified rooms, or pursue the relevant approvals.
recommendations.business_case: FALCO 2 11.7 (UL Class I Zone 1) and Riken (explosion-proof) publish approvals; ThermGAS documents do not.
recommendations.limitation: Area classification is site-specific; engineering review needed.
recommendations.next_step: Confirm with ThermGAS engineering which installations are permitted.

recommendations.title: Build the lifecycle-cost case with real quotes
recommendations.action: Collect quotes for FALCO 2 11.7 lamps and service, RKI filling monitors, and ThermGAS configurations for the same room (same number of points).
recommendations.business_case: Point PIDs are cheap to buy ($3,521 list) but need a lamp every ~4 months; one Haloguard IR can cover up to 24 points. The net effect is unknown until priced.
recommendations.limitation: Lamp, labor and ThermGAS prices are Not Publicly Available - no TCO is claimed in this dashboard.
recommendations.next_step: Request three quotations; use the dashboard's scenario fields only with documented inputs.

recommendations.business_case: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference; a documented pilot becomes the proof every later proposal needs.
recommendations.limitation: Requires plant access and sponsor resources.

meta.title: ThermGAS U.S. Competitive Intelligence - executive layer
meta.status_note: Everything in this file is a research-team PROPOSAL for management consideration. It is not an approved ThermGAS strategy, budget or commitment. Evidence labels: Verified / Inferred / Assumption / Unknown.

core_conclusion.headline: ThermGAS has a credible opening as the DMC-specific, lamp-free concentration monitor that complements event detection, but it cannot yet prove it. Its own DMC specification is inconsistent and no vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant reference.
core_conclusion.next_move: Proposal for management: run a 30-day evidence sprint (fix the DMC spec, answer the hazardous-area question, get real quotes) before committing any pilot hardware or sales spend.

known.text: Two direct competitors sell DMC-capable fixed monitors to battery makers: ION Science FALCO 2 11.7 and Riken Keiki / RKI.
ThermGAS's DMC detection figure conflicts across its own documents (0.5 ppm vs 1 ppm) and DMC is missing from its Master Gas List.
No public U.S. battery-plant DMC customer reference was found for any vendor (absence after search, not proof of absence).
The FALCO 2 11.7 UV lamp lasts up to 4 months (3-month lamp warranty).

inferred.text: PAIR should be more selective for DMC than a PID in mixed-solvent rooms (principle only; no matched test exists).
Honeywell's off-gas event detection is complementary to, not a substitute for, DMC concentration monitoring.
A Georgia-based service model could be an advantage in the Southeast (not tested).

assumed.text: Battery-plant buyers will budget for both an event layer and a concentration layer.
MSA could add DMC to its PAIR-based Chillgard platform.
Large Asian-OEM plants may standardize on Riken globally.

core_conclusion.short: ThermGAS can win as the DMC-specific, lamp-free monitor, but it has to prove its own spec first.
core_conclusion.short_next: Proposal: 30-day evidence sprint before any pilot spend.

key_findings.title: The race is against two named rivals, and neither is unbeatable
key_findings.body: ION Science is cheap to buy ($3,521 list) and hazardous-area approved, but needs a UV lamp roughly every 4 months and cannot tell DMC from other solvents. Riken has the broadest battery portfolio and a claimed 10,000+ detectors in Li-ion plants worldwide, but publishes no DMC detection limit.
key_findings.so_what: A buyer will compare ThermGAS with these two first. ThermGAS wins only with a test-conditioned DMC spec.
key_findings.short: Two direct rivals: ION Science (cheap, lamp change about every 4 months) and Riken (broad, no DMC limit published).

key_findings.title: The U.S. reference-site position is still open
key_findings.body: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant DMC reference. Honeywell sells gigafactory event detection but reports a rate, not DMC concentration.
key_findings.so_what: The first documented plant pilot would be a lasting differentiator, and Honeywell is better treated as a partner-style complement than a head-on rival.
key_findings.short: No vendor has a public U.S. battery-plant reference yet. The first one is a lasting differentiator.

key_findings.title: ThermGAS's own evidence is the main blocker
key_findings.body: Conflicting DMC spec, no interference data, no product-level hazardous-area rating (the Energy page claims Class I Div 1/2 enclosures without naming a model), no battery reference and no public price. Competitors publish approvals.
key_findings.so_what: These are cheap to fix compared with a sales push, and they decide whether any pilot is credible.
key_findings.short: ThermGAS's own gaps (0.5 vs 1 ppm spec, no product-level hazardous-area rating) are the main blocker.

notes.text: Photoacoustic infrared fits the first row. Hydrides are dominated by colorimetric tape systems and are not ThermGAS's market.

note.title: Ethylene oxide rules are being relaxed
note.text: In July 2025 the administration exempted 41 facilities from EPA's 2024 sterilizer rule, and in March 2026 EPA proposed letting sterilizers choose continuous or parametric monitoring. Workplace exposure limits still apply, which is why this page does not lead with ethylene oxide.
